notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: nine morphometric measurements on 104 mountain brushtail possums trapped at seven sites (Lindenmayer et al. 1995). The page and the book's code (Maindonald, Braun and Andrews 2024, jhmaindonald.github.io/Rcode, subsection 1.2.1 and chapter 9) only plot, bootstrap a correlation, run principal components and a linear discriminant analysis of site, and fit no model. Possums repeat within trapping site, so site groups the rows (a cluster the source treats as independent, as ROS). Total length is the measurement subsection 1.2.1 compares by sex and Pop (bwplot(Pop ~ totlngth | sex)); Pop classifies the sites (Victoria against the rest) and is a site-level covariate. The other eight measurements are alternate responses; age is a usable column. RULE GAP: site is also the class the discriminant analysis predicts (crabs and iris were excluded as discrimination tables), but here it indexes the sampling cluster. Hand check #162: stands; seven sites of 7 to 33 possums.

psymetadata documents the data only (no example, no vignette): 85 Fisher-z effect sizes of the out-group entitativity and prejudice relation from 21 studies (study_id), es_id one per row. Agadullina and Lovakov (2018, Br J Soc Psychol 57:703-731) pool 85 effects from 33 independent samples (abstract via search); their model was not read (paywalled). Effects nested in studies rendered as a three-level model, es_id the observation-level term. vi is the sampling variance, which the source weights by; n enters it. Hand check #162: the paper clusters the 85 effects by 33 independent samples, an identifier the table omits (21 study_id labels), so the study and effect intercepts stay the reader's proposal.

psymetadata documents the data only (no example, no vignette; source OSF jhavp): 637 Hedges' g effect sizes of Cogmed working-memory training from 48 studies (study_id), es_id one per row, moderators transfer, test, allocation, comparison, baseline, age group and population. Aksayli, Sala and Gobet (2019, Educ Res Rev 27:229-243) not read (full text unavailable); the group's other meta-analyses use robust variance estimation. Effects nested in studies rendered as a three-level model. vi is the sampling variance, which the source weights by; ni enters it. Hand check #162: the authors' code (osf.io/sbjn2) fits robu() with hierarchical weights, which state a between-study and a within-study variance, separately by transfer (near, far) and follow-up; no column holds follow-up, so the formula pools both. Its moderator regressions have the same response and grouping, so they file no row; its model of the baseline effect is no row, since a baseline is a covariate.

RESPONSE INFERRED: the published response is a signed rating no column holds. Readme (osf.io/download/cyns9); Duyan and Balci 2018 Psychon Bull Rev 25(4), Experiment 2 (targets 7 and 11). The abstract: "Individual linear regression fits as well as the linear mixed model with a fixed effect of reproduced numerosity on confidence ratings, and participants as independent random effects on the intercept and the slope revealed significant positive slopes for all the target numerosities". Hand check #162: the paper fits the signed confidence-directionality rating, separately for Stimulus 7 and 11, and ErrorDirectionJudgment is -1 on all 5,917 rows, so the published rating cannot be rebuilt; Confidence with the uncorrelated subject slope is the reader's proposal. Response is the reproduced count (beeps before the stop), Error = Response - Stimulus; ErrorDirectionJudgment holds one value (-1) in this file.

psymetadata documents the data only (OSF 34xyw): 316 Hedges' g effects of shared reading on children's language from 54 studies (study_id), es_id one per row, moderators measure, age, ses, experimenter, duration, dialogic_reading and follow_up. Noble et al. (2019, Educ Res Rev 28:100290; full text read): we used robust variance estimation (RVE) with hierarchical weights and small-sample corrections to calculate the overall effect size and run meta-regression (Hedges, Tipton and Johnson 2010), the effect sizes of one study forming one cluster, in the robumeta R package. Hand check #162: the authors' code (osf.io/ebcg3) fits robu() separately at post-test and follow-up (follow_up N and Y, 268 and 48 effects), and rma.mv with a study intercept for the category means; its moderator fits have the same response and grouping, so they file no row.

Read Keuleers, Lacey, Rastle and Brysbaert 2012 (Behav Res Methods 44, PMC3278621) and OSF b5sdk. Lexical decision megastudy, 78 participants; "a random permutation of the list was split in two", each half given to the odd- or even-ranked participants, with nonwords made per list, so participants and items (spelling) are partly crossed. The paper analyzes its virtual experiments and Monte Carlo power simulation "in a linear mixed effects model with crossed random effects for participants and items" on RT, analyses limited to word trials; their fixed effects are item norms or a virtual condition outside this table, so the table's model keeps the intercept. Hand check #162: published_model no, since the paper's models hold predictors this table lacks; the random part alone is the reader's proposal. rt is NA for outliers and errors (rt.raw the raw time); subset lexicality == "W". trial is the stimulus id (one spelling per id); accuracy, response and button restate the decision, previous.rt and previous.accuracy lag the response.

Read Keuleers, Diependaele and Brysbaert 2010 (Front Psychol 1:174) and OSF uw7t6. 39 participants, "the participants in our study responded to all stimuli", so participants and items (spelling) are fully crossed. Virtual experiments: "RTs from correct responses between 200 ms and lower than 1500 ms were then analyzed with a mixed effects model with condition as a fixed effect and crossed random effects of participants and stimuli"; the condition and the Monte Carlo predictors (log frequency and its square) are item properties outside this table, so the table's model keeps the intercept. Hand check #162: published_model no, since the paper's models hold predictors this table lacks; the random part alone is the reader's proposal. Subset lexicality == "W", accuracy == 1, 200 <= rt < 1500. trial is the stimulus id; row 2 is the practice analysis on zscore.

Read Brysbaert, Stevens, Mandera and Keuleers 2016 (J Exp Psychol Hum Percept Perform 42(3), osf.io/download/4p65k) and OSF jfkvw. dlp2_trials0 is list 0 (40 participants) of the trial table split in two files, dlp2_trials1 list 1; each participant saw every word and nonword of the list, so participant and item are fully crossed within the file. Footnote 9: "run mixed effects models on the complete dataset ... We aborted the lme4() R program after 10 days of running, but were able to run the analysis on the new package developed by Bates in Julia ... The results were comparable"; its predictors are the word norms of the item-level regressions (frequency, length, syllables, age of acquisition, concreteness, OLD20, prevalence), outside this table, and its random terms are not stated (participants and items assumed). Hand check #162: published_model no, since footnote 9's model holds predictors this table lacks and states no random terms; the participant and item intercepts are the reader's proposal. RT analyses use blocks 3 to 62 (warmup == 0); rtC is the RT of correct trials after removing items under 65% accuracy and adjusted-boxplot outliers per block, participant and lexicality; rtR raw, rate = 1000/RT, z per participant and block and I imputed versions in ignore. Words only (lexicality == "W"); spelling restates item, pair links a word to its matched nonword.

Readme (osf.io/download/xenqp); Kantner and Lindsay 2010 Mem Cognit 38(4), Experiment 4 (full text not read; no mixed model known). Rahnev et al. 2020 fit no model per file. Recognition memory of words; between subjects, Condition crosses the size rule (big, small, mixed) with trial-by-trial feedback, whose effect on sensitivity is the Stimulus:Condition interaction. RULE GAP: the 1-6 rating from "Definitely Not Studied" to "Definitely Studied" (Raw_Response) is filed as the response instead of the folded Confidence (1-3), since the database derives both Response (old/new) and Confidence from it; Stimulus (old 1, new 0) carries recognition sensitivity. StimulusType is constant (Word). Hand check #162: stands; Raw_Response is the elicited 1-6 judgment and Confidence its fold; 78 participants of 150 trials.
